AD.name: Andorra
AD.summary: Possessing drugs for own use is a crime (prison up to 1 year or arrest, plus fine); cannabis is a minor offence (arrest or fine). A new Penal Code (Llei 18/2026) raises the fines from mid-December 2026.

emergency.poisonNote: No national poison centre found; call SUM 116. Spain's SIT (+34 91 562 04 20, 24h) is the nearest Spanish-language centre.

AD.callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law. Own-use possession is a crime, so police involvement is possible. Failing to help or call for help for someone in grave danger is an offence.

lsd.note: Own-use possession is a crime: prison up to 1 year or arrest, plus fine up to €1,200 (2 years in public venues). New Code from mid-Dec 2026: fine €1,000–2,000.

AL.name: Albania
AL.summary: Possession for personal use 'in small doses' is excluded from the drug-dealing offence (Criminal Code art. 283) but read narrowly (about one dose); more is prosecuted as dealing (5–10 yrs). Art. 283 is under review.

emergency.poisonNote: No poison information centre is listed in WHO's 2023 directory; the QSUT 'Mother Teresa' hospital in Tirana has a clinical toxicology service.

AL.callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law or other specific legal protection for people who call for help in an overdose was found.

lsd.note: UN Schedule I. Own use in small doses isn't a crime (CC art. 283), read narrowly; more is prosecuted as dealing (5–10 yrs).

AM.name: Armenia
AM.summary: Using drugs without a prescription or possessing small amounts is an administrative offence (fines, higher if repeated within a year); larger amounts are crimes. Seeking treatment voluntarily avoids liability for use.

emergency.poisonNote: No poison information centre is listed for Armenia in WHO's 2023 directory; call 911 or 103 (112 also works from mobiles).

AM.callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law. People who voluntarily ask a medical facility for help with drug use are released from administrative liability for use.

AT.name: Austria
AT.summary: Possession is a crime under the SMG, but personal-use cases go to health authorities and prosecutors must suspend them ("Therapie statt Strafe"). The NPS law punishes only supply. Drug checking is legal.
AT.callingForHelp: Ambulance (144) staff are bound by confidentiality and police are not routinely informed; personal-use offences go to health authorities first. No Good Samaritan law.
AT.drugChecking: Legal and available: checkit! (Vienna, fixed site and events) and Z6 drug checking (Innsbruck).

CH.name: Switzerland
CH.summary: Four-pillar policy (prevention, therapy, harm reduction, enforcement). Adults: up to 10 g cannabis is not punishable and use is a CHF 100 ticket; other drug use is a fined contravention. Drug checking is legal.
CH.callingForHelp: Ambulance (144) staff are bound by medical secrecy and police are not routinely called. Health and social workers need not report drug use (Art. 3c BetmG). No Good Samaritan law.
CH.drugChecking: Legal, organised by cantons and cities: fixed and mobile services, e.g. in Zurich, Bern, Basel, Geneva and Lucerne.

GB.name: United Kingdom
GB.summary: Misuse of Drugs Act 1971 (Classes A/B/C): possessing controlled drugs is a crime. Psychoactive Substances Act 2016 bans supplying other highs (possession legal outside prisons). Drug checking needs a Home Office licence.
GB.callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law. Ambulance crews don't routinely call police; many forces attend overdoses only if there is a death, violence or risk to crews. NHS confidentiality applies.
GB.drugChecking: Legal only under Home Office licence: The Loop (Bristol, London, events) and WEDINOS (Wales, anonymous postal testing).

GE.name: Georgia
GE.summary: Very strict, toughened in 2025. Using cannabis in private isn't punished and ≤5 g is an administrative offence, but most other drugs have no or tiny 'small amount' limits, so possession is usually a crime.

IE.drugChecking: HSE runs free, anonymous 'back of house' drug checking at some festivals (Safer Nightlife, since 2022). No fixed-site service.

IT.summary: Possessing any drug for personal use is an administrative offence (licence/passport suspension, DPR 309/90 art. 75); supply is a crime. Hemp-flower sales banned in 2025. No legal drug-checking framework.
IT.callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law. Personal-use possession is not a crime, so health staff have no duty to report it and are bound by secrecy. Failing to help someone in danger is an offence (c.p. art. 593).
IT.drugChecking: No national legal framework; a few regional outreach projects (e.g. Neutravel, Piedmont) offer checking at events.

RU.name: Russia
RU.summary: Very harsh. Below a tiny 'significant amount' (e.g. 6 g cannabis, 0.2 g cocaine) possession or use is an administrative offence (fine or up to 15 days' jail; foreigners expelled). Above it: up to 3, 3–10 or 10–15 yrs.
RU.callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan protection. Hospitals report crime-linked injuries, so police may follow up; narcology registration is possible. Seeking treatment voluntarily avoids admin liability for use.
RU.drugChecking: No drug checking services. Sharing drug information can be prosecuted as 'propaganda' (Code of Administrative Offences art. 6.13).

lsd.note: 'Significant amount' is 0.0001 g (0.1 mg) and whole mixtures can be weighed, so even one blotter can mean prosecution; 0.005 g is 'large' (3–10 yrs).

SE.drugChecking: No drug checking services; there is no legal exemption for testing drugs outside police and forensic labs.

SI.name: Slovenia
SI.summary: Possessing any drug for personal use is a misdemeanour (fine), not a crime; a lower fine or none is possible for a one-off small amount or if you enter treatment. Supply is a crime. Free, legal drug checking (DrogArt).
SI.callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law, but possession for own use is only a misdemeanour and medical staff are bound by confidentiality. Police may attend if there is a death or violence.
SI.drugChecking: Legal and free: DrogArt runs anonymous drug checking in Ljubljana and Maribor (lab analysis by NLZOH) and reagent testing.

lsd.note: Possession for own use: misdemeanour fine (roughly €40–210), lower for a one-off small amount. Selling or sharing is a crime.

SM.summary: Own law (L. 139/1997): possessing drugs without intent to sell, and personal use, are crimes (6 months–3 years, reducible); adults with under 3 g of cannabis face a day-fine. Tables updated Sept 2026.

emergency.poisonNote: No national poison centre; the nearest are Italian centres (e.g. Milan Niguarda, +39 02 6610 1029, 24h).

UA.name: Ukraine
UA.summary: A 'small amount' for own use is an administrative offence (fine, community work or up to 15 days' arrest); more is a crime. Many limits are tiny (cocaine 0.02 g, LSD 10 µg). Medical cannabis legal since Aug 2024.
UA.callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law. Medical confidentiality applies, but police may be involved. Voluntarily starting drug treatment exempts from criminal liability for basic possession (CC art. 309(4)).
UA.drugChecking: No established public drug checking service is known; its legal status is unclear.

lsd.note: 'Small amount' is only 0.00001 g (10 µg), less than one tab, so typical amounts are a crime (fine, probation or restriction of liberty; more: prison).

emergency.poisonNote: No poison information centre is listed in WHO's 2023 directory; call 112 or 194.
